title: Ebola cases reach Kenya and Nigeria as child deaths rise

needs.need: The cumulative number of Ebola cases and how much of DR Congo the outbreak covers.
needs.accepts: A cumulative case count for the outbreak in DR Congo and the number of affected provinces, tied to a reporting date and credited to a named source.

example.value: Nearly 11,000 confirmed cases had been reported across eight provinces of DR Congo by 11 November 2026.
example.source: WHO Director-General's remarks at the Member State briefing (2026-11-11)

needs.need: The outbreak's overall death rate, against which to read the seven-in-ten figure for children under five.
needs.accepts: A named source's overall share of cases that died in this outbreak, or case and death totals from the same place and date that give it.

example.value: Nearly 11,000 confirmed cases and more than 5,300 deaths had been reported in DR Congo, roughly half as many deaths as cases.
example.source: WHO Director-General's remarks at the Member State briefing (2026-11-11)

needs.need: When the outbreak was declared and how long the response has been running.
needs.accepts: States that the outbreak was announced in mid-May 2026 (about six months before the story), naming a source.

example.value: The outbreak has spread to eight of Congo's 26 provinces since it was announced in mid-May.

needs.need: How insecurity is obstructing efforts to find cases and stop transmission.
needs.accepts: A named source saying that attacks or insecurity are limiting health teams' access to communities and disrupting the response, such as contact tracing, surveillance or treatment.

example.value: Attacks and insecurity were obstructing the Ebola response and limiting access to communities; more than 1,000 contacts were no longer being followed up.

needs.need: What capacity has been added to detect Ebola infections.
needs.inStory: The rise from two testing labs to more than two dozen gives health teams more ways to identify infections and guide outbreak control.
needs.accepts: A named source reporting that laboratories able to test for the virus rose from two to more than two dozen.

example.value: The number of laboratories able to test for the virus increased from two to more than two dozen.
example.source: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, as reported by UN News (2026-11-17)

needs.need: When the two Bundibugyo-specific vaccine candidates are due to enter testing.
needs.inStory: Two vaccine candidates designed for this Ebola virus are due to enter a trial, offering a possible tool against future spread but not yet proven protection.
needs.accepts: A named source saying two Bundibugyo-specific candidates are due to join an ongoing vaccine trial in the coming weeks, as a trial, not a rollout.

example.value: Two candidate vaccines developed specifically for Bundibugyo virus were due to be added to an ongoing vaccine trial in the coming weeks.
example.source: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, as reported by UN News (2026-11-17)

needs.need: What Bundibugyo virus is and why existing Ebola vaccines are not known to protect against it.
needs.accepts: Explains, crediting a named medical or public-health source, that Bundibugyo is one of several distinct viruses causing Ebola disease and that the licensed vaccines target Zaire ebolavirus, so protection against Bundibugyo is not established.

example.value: Bundibugyo and Zaire are distinct viruses that cause Ebola disease; the licensed Ebola vaccines target Zaire ebolavirus and have not been shown to protect against Bundibugyo virus.
example.source: World Health Organization, Ebola disease fact sheet

needs.need: The scale of ongoing weekly transmission, set against the few cases reported abroad.
needs.inStory: The available figures show hundreds of new cases weekly, not millions of people affected.
needs.accepts: A current count or range of new cases per week, credited to a named source and kept apart from cumulative cases and imported-case totals.

example.value: Between 400 and 500 new cases were still being reported each week.
example.source: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, as reported by UN News (2026-11-17)

notes: The key covers the Ebola item, the story's headline; the story's brief lines on hormone-disrupting chemicals and an EU migration proposal are not developed enough to need context. Deaths over cases is a crude comparison, not a matched-age analysis. Case totals differ slightly between WHO (nearly 11,000 confirmed) and Congo's government data (more than 11,000 recorded); either, dated and credited, meets the scale need.
